checked_claims: Normalized crossover and marginalized mutation probabilities, with explicit zero-mass fallback
TSP feasibility given complete graph and nonempty feasible base-policy support
Positive rank weights and stochastic replacement scope
Routing code mask union, mutation and separate best-so-far result
Experimental exceptions, local-search disclosures and budget scope

independent_scope_check.source_and_assumptions: Independently compared source physical pp.3-4 Eqs.(2)-(5), complete-graph TSP support conditions, and p.9 limitations against the report and coverage.
independent_scope_check.decisive_scope_check: For Z>0 the masked policy sums to one and mu*p+(1-mu)*p_A sums to one; for Z=0 the separately stated fallback p is required. With positive feasible base support, induction over unvisited nodes gives a tour on the complete graph, without an optimality implication. Positive kappa makes every inverse-rank weight finite, including rank zero. The 0.38,0.57,0.05 example follows directly by arithmetic. The existing six-city output is a finite illustration, correctly labeled as such, not a universal proof.
independent_scope_check.counterevidence_and_limits: Source p.9 explicitly disclaims convergence/distribution guarantees. Stochastic elitism is not deterministic preservation of the working-population best; the report distinguishes separately stored best-so-far. The report does not extrapolate routing checks to language/molecule pipelines, empirical superiority, toxicity, chemistry, or solver/data provenance. Coverage marks those limits and image-only gaps explicitly.
independent_scope_check.conclusion: No Issue Found is accepted only for the declared normalization, feasible support and selected routing mechanics. No new substantive problem or repair is supported by this focused scope/honesty check.
